title: Backpack Feature Explorer with Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D backpack feature explorer using Three.js. Load the 3D model 'coffeemat.glb' using GLTFLoader to represent the product in the scene.

SCENE SETUP:
- Set up a Three.js scene with a dark gradient background (top: #1a1a2e, bottom: #16213e).
- Add a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.5, 4) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and two directional lights: one warm from upper-left (0xffeedd, intensity 0.8) and one cool from lower-right (0xaaccff, intensity 0.5).
- Load 'coffeemat.glb' using GLTFLoader. Center and scale the model so it fits within a 2-unit bounding box. Place it at the origin.
- Add a subtle circular ground plane (radius 2, dark gray #222233) beneath the model.
- The model should slowly auto-rotate around the Y-axis at 0.3 rad/s.

FEATURE HOTSPOTS:
- Create 3 clickable hotspot markers (small glowing spheres, radius 0.08) positioned around the model at:
  - Hotspot 1 ('Material'): position (0.5, 1.0, 0.5), color yellow (#ffdd00)
  - Hotspot 2 ('Compartments'): position (-0.5, 0.5, 0.5), color cyan (#00ddff)
  - Hotspot 3 ('Straps'): position (0, 1.5, -0.3), color magenta (#ff00dd)
- Hotspots should pulse (scale oscillation between 0.8 and 1.2) to attract attention.
- Hotspots should be children of the model so they rotate with it.

PARTICLE EFFECTS:
- When a hotspot is clicked, spawn a burst of 50 particles from the hotspot position.
- Particles should be small spheres or points that expand outward in random directions, fade out over 1.5 seconds, and then are removed.
- Particle color should match the clicked hotspot color.
- Track whether particles are currently active.

UI ELEMENTS:
- Add a title 'Backpack Feature Explorer' at the top center of the page (white text, 24px).
- Add an info panel (div, id='info-panel') at the bottom center. Initially it shows 'Click a hotspot to explore features'. When a hotspot is clicked, it shows the feature name and a short description:
  - Material: 'Premium waterproof nylon with reinforced stitching'
  - Compartments: 'Three spacious compartments with padded laptop sleeve'
  - Straps: 'Ergonomic padded straps with adjustable chest buckle'
- Add a 'Reset View' button (id='reset-btn') in the top-right corner that resets the camera to its initial position and clears the info panel back to default text.
- Add a 'Toggle Rotation' button (id='toggle-rotation-btn') that pauses/resumes the auto-rotation.

INTERACTION:
- Use raycasting on click to detect hotspot hits.
- Clicking empty space does nothing.
- Implement OrbitControls for manual camera manipulation (but auto-rotation takes over when enabled).

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields:
  - modelLoaded: boolean, true once the GLB model is fully loaded
  - autoRotating: boolean, true when auto-rotation is active (starts true)
  - rotationAngle: number, current Y rotation of the model in radians
  - activeFeature: string, name of the currently selected feature ('none' initially, then 'Material', 'Compartments', or 'Straps')
  - particlesActive: boolean, true when particle burst is currently animating
  - particleCount: number, current number of active particles in the scene
  - hotspotCount: number, should be 3
  - cameraDistance: number, distance from camera to origin
- Update these values every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Particles should move outward from the hotspot with random velocity vectors (speed 1-3 units/s), decelerate slightly due to drag, and fade out linearly over 1.5 seconds. Auto-rotation is constant angular velocity. No gravity needed for particles—they expand radially.
